summary: The Gambia admits ECOWAS citizens, most Commonwealth nationals and much of northern Europe visa-free — visitors are stamped in for 28 days, which can be extended twice by 28 days in Banjul (ECOWAS citizens may stay up to 90 days) — while US, French and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.

vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — commonly checked for arrivals overland or via mainland West Africa.

travelInsurance.text: No official source states a travel insurance requirement for entry to The Gambia. Cover is recommended — medical facilities are basic and serious cases are evacuated to Dakar or Europe.

source.name: Gambia Immigration Department

onwardTicket.text: No official source states an onward or return ticket requirement for entry to The Gambia. Airlines flying into Banjul may check return tickets, and border officers may ask about onward travel.

source.name: Gambia Immigration Department

proofOfFunds.text: No official source states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for The Gambia. Border officers may ask visitors to show means of support and accommodation details.

source.name: Gambia Immigration Department

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states The Gambia's currency declaration threshold or limits on taking dalasi out. Declare large sums of cash to customs on arrival.

source.name: Gambia Immigration Department

payments.text: Resort hotels and a few coastal restaurants take cards; everywhere else is cash. Bring GBP, EUR or USD to change into dalasi — ATMs cluster around the Senegambia strip and Banjul and are unreliable up-country.

safety.text: The Gambia is one of West Africa's calmer destinations and most visits are trouble-free. Petty theft and persistent hustling by "bumsters" on tourist beaches are the main annoyances; use registered taxis at night.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Gambia travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is dry and sunny — peak season for the beaches and superb birdwatching along the river; the June-to-October rains bring humidity and mosquitoes.

tips.text: Unless you are an ECOWAS citizen (up to 90 days), border officers stamp you in for 28 days whatever your visa status — for longer stays, extend at the Immigration Department in Banjul before the stamp expires.
Malaria is present year-round. Take prophylaxis, sleep under nets outside resort hotels and use repellent, especially during and after the rains.
Expect friendly but persistent "bumsters" offering guiding and companionship on the beaches. A firm, polite refusal works; official green-shirted guides are the licensed alternative.
Day trips into Senegal are popular, but check Senegal's entry rules for your passport and make sure your Gambian stay allows re-entry. Carry your passport at the ferry and border crossings.
Bring enough hard currency for your whole stay. Cards rarely work outside big hotels, and dalasi are difficult to obtain or exchange outside The Gambia.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS states, most Commonwealth countries and much of northern and western Europe — including the UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Scandinavia — enter visa-free; visitors are stamped in for 28 days, ECOWAS citizens for up to 90. US, French, Portuguese and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Yes — US passport holders must obtain a visa in advance, normally from the Gambian Embassy in Washington, DC. Confirm current fees and processing times with the embassy before booking.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Gambia?
faq.answer: Border officers stamp visitors in for 28 days whatever their visa status; ECOWAS citizens can stay up to 90 days under the Community's free-movement protocol. Stays can be extended twice, by 28 days each time, at the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area. Apply before your stamp expires.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — which includes most of mainland West Africa, so overland travelers from Senegal should carry the certificate. Direct arrivals from Europe do not need it.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit The Gambia?
faq.answer: November to April — the dry season — brings reliable sunshine for the Atlantic beaches and the best birdwatching along the River Gambia. The rainy season from June to October is quieter, greener and more humid.
